What it means: The Boston Licensing Board held a virtual hearing on October 13, 2026 [00:38], to review alleged violations involving local businesses [01:40]. The hearing covered Little Haiti International Cuisine operating past legal closing hours on July 5, 2026 [01:55-02:00], Lazuri Cafe allowing patrons on its patio after hours on August 12 and September 11, 2026 [18:51-18:54, 24:36-24:41], and Lolita Cocina & Tequila Bar regarding a patron assault involving a glass and failure to report the incident to police on August 29, 2026 [15:28-15:42]. The board did not issue immediate rulings or penalties, placing all items under advisement [15:15, 24:25, 28:48, 39:38].

Who moved it: The hearing was chaired by Kathleen Joyce alongside Commissioners Kiana Saxon and Ava Concepcion [00:56-01:02]. Police reports and details were presented by Sergeant John McNulty [02:14], Officer Lopez [29:39], Sergeant Detective William Gallagher [31:16], and Sergeant Carl DeGoff [19:21]. Licensees offering testimony included manager George Anthony Cran for Little Haiti International Cuisine [02:24], owner Rifat Tenka for Lazuri Cafe [19:11], and attorney William Burke, general manager Gar McLean, and owner Mark Malatesta for Lolita Cocina & Tequila Bar [15:48-15:57, 33:40, 38:28].

What to watch: The board is scheduled to vote on these cases on Thursday at 12:00 p.m. noon, which is a departure from its typical 10:00 a.m. time [39:46-39:53]. Official notices and meeting recordings will be posted to the City of Boston website [00:48, 39:53]. Final decisions regarding potential warnings or license suspensions are not settled in this transcript and will depend on Thursday's vote [15:15, 39:46].

summary: The Boston Licensing Board held a hearing to review several premise violations. The board first discussed a violation for Little Haiti International Cuisine operating past legal closing hours [01:58], where the licensee cited safety concerns following a nearby shooting [05:17], [08:51], and the board took the matter under advisement [15:16]. Next, the board reviewed two separate incidents involving Turkish Lazuri Cafe regarding an unposted entertainment license and patrons occupying the outdoor patio past closing hours [18:54], [25:22]; after the owner explained takeout procedures and efforts to block off patio seating [22:05], [26:08], the board took both violations under advisement [24:25], [28:48]. Finally, the board examined an assault and battery with a dangerous weapon and failure to call police at Lolita Cocina & Tequila Bar [15:30], [15:38], where the board evaluated security responses and updated staff reporting policies [37:41], [38:51] before taking the matter under advisement [39:38]. The board concluded by announcing that its upcoming decision meeting was rescheduled for Thursday at 12:00 p.m. [39:51].
